days.text:
/    
◆ 7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer 
and Kahi). 
◆ Head to The Iraq Museum and wander in its galleries that will take 
us in a journey of civilizations of Iraq through the time.  
◆ Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local 
markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - 
the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and 
antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”. 
◆ Visit heritage sites such as Ma drasa Mustansiriya School and the 
Abbasid Palace. 
◆ This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigris river and an 
explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi. 
◆ Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder 
Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or 
any other of your favourites. We also will grab a treat from both Al 
Shahbender cafe and Haj Zbala Juice shop. 
◆ Free time in the afternoon to explore the modern parts of Baghdad.  
Overnight: Baghdad / night 1.

/ 
◆ After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage 
site. 
◆ We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, 
the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old 
temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, 
the place where Alexander the Great passed away.  
◆ We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces 
that was built during the past regime time with special access to the 
upper floors. 
◆ Traditional lunch options that you can choose from. 
◆ Time to visit Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known 
as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of 
Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a 
religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu. 
◆ After that, we will drive to Nasiriyah. 
Overnight: Nasiriyah / night 2.

/ 
◆ At 5:00 AM we will then drive to Chibayesh and have a marshland 
experience.  
◆ Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.  
◆ Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the 
Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos, reed, plants, and meeting 
the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world 
and a UNESCO world heritage site. 
◆ After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq 
which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch will take place in the 
reed house - Al Mudhif. 
◆ Stories from local people “Al Madan” who  have adapted to life on 
the water over the centuries. 
◆ Then, we will drive to the historical city of Ur to visit the Great 
Ziggurat of Ur, a UNESCO world heritage site and the former capital 
of Mesopotamia during the Sumerian time.  (2 Hour drive) 
◆ The site includes Sholgi palace, and the oldest arch of its kind in the 
world at the entrance of Dub-Lal-Makh temple. 
◆ Head back to Baghdad. 
Overnight: Baghdad/ night 3.

/ 
◆ After breakfast, we will head to visit The Ziggurat of Dur -Kurigalzu 
and Enlil temples which are dedicated to Sumerian gods. The 
Ziggurat was unusually well preserved, standing to a height of about 
fifty-two metres. 
◆ Following that, we will visit Taq Kasra “the Arch of Ctesiphon” - the 
largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork according to the 
world history of architecture, served as a royal capital of the Parthian 
and Sasanian empires.  
◆ We can witness the sunset from the neglected panorama building.  
Overnight: Baghdad/ night 4.

/ 
◆ 7 30 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful 
Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, 
lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is 
a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 
◆ After that we will head to Hatra, an important historic religious centre 
with its strategic position along caravan trade routes. Hatra was one 
of the first Arab states to be established outside of Arabia. Lunch 
will be in the middle of the way in one of the village's restaurants.  
◆ Head to Mosul, check into the hotel and have the famous dish (Lahm 
Baajeen) for dinner. 
◆ Free time in Mosul and visiting the cafe house for local music 
performance. This place used to be a hospital for ISIS during the 
battles. 
Overnight: Mosul / night 5.

/  
◆ 8 AM Start the day with discovering the reconstruction of the old city, 
especially Al-Nuri Mosque, Al Hadbaa Minaret and Al Tahira church 
that are being rebuilt by UNESCO. 
◆ Walk through the area where the last and most intensive battle 
against ISIS took place. 
◆ Hear stories from the individuals who lived through the war.  
◆ The famous “Kubba of Mosul” for lunch which is a delicious meal 
made by locals. 
◆ After that, we will head to Lalish and have a unique experience with 
the Yazidis of Iraq, and learn about their  most holy and important 
land.  
Overnight: Duhok / night 6.

/ 
◆ After breakfast, we will head to Shanidar Cave, one of the earliest 
locations where Neanderthal Remains were discovered.  
◆ Head to Soran. 
◆ Soran, a city surrounded by mountains. In Soran we will get to see 
the iconic Gali Ali Beg Waterfall that was illustrated to one of the 
Iraqi bills. In addition to the beautiful landscape around the city.  
◆ Ride the Teleferric up Korek Mountain and enjoy the views of the 
surrounding landscape. 
◆ Head to Rawanduz that it’s known for its striking scenery, and 
enjoying the view of the canyon.  
◆ See the Hamilton road, a stunning feat of engineering.  
◆ Head to Erbil for an overnight. 
Overnight: Erbil / Night 7.

: Arrival in Basra
Upon your arrival at Basra International Airport, you will be assisted with the Fast-track Visa process. Our representative will meet you at the exit for a private transfer to your hotel (approx. 30–45 minutes) for check-in. The remainder of the day is at your leisure to rest and settle in. Overnight in Basra.

: Basra City Tour
After breakfast, we begin our exploration of the "Venice of the East." We start by visiting the Basra Museum, housed in one of the grand former presidential palaces. Next, we enjoy a scenic river tour in Shatt Al-Arab on traditional Ashari boats, followed by a relaxing walk along the Basra Corniche. We will then explore Old Basra, famous for its historic Shanasheel houses (traditional wooden balconies) and the Ashar Canal. Depending on the time, we will also visit the vibrant Old Basra Bazaar. The evening concludes with a traditional seafood dinner, showcasing Basra's famous local flavors. Overnight in Basra.

We could also add The mosque of Khutwa Al Imam Ali in Zubair, which is only 40-50 mins away from the center of the current city of Basra. The area is named after  Zubayr ibn al-Awwam whom is a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad. A visit to his tomb is also possible.

: Qurna, Chibayesh Marshlands & The Ancient City of Ur
At 05:00 AM Timing can vary depending on the sunrise time at the date of the tour, we begin our journey by heading to Qurna (approx. 1.5 hours), the legendary meeting point of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. Here, we will explore the Tree of Adam, an ancient holy tree mentioned in biblical traditions. We then drive to Chibayesh (approx. 1 hour) for an authentic Marshland experience. You will enjoy a local breakfast in a traditional mud house with a local family, followed by a boat tour through the floating villages of the Ahwar (a UNESCO World Heritage site). You will witness the unique ecosystem of reeds, water buffaloes, and migratory birds, and hear fascinating stories from the Al-Madan people who have adapted to life on the water for centuries. After the marshland tour, we drive to the historical City of Ur (approx. 1.5 hours). You will visit the Great Ziggurat of Ur, the former capital of Mesopotamia. The tour includes the House of Prophet Abraham, Shulgi Palace, and the oldest known arch at the entrance of the Dub-Lal-Makh Temple. We will stay to witness one of the most beautiful sunsets over the Sumerian ruins. Overnight in Nasiriyah.

: The Ancient City of Uruk & Najaf
After breakfast, we begin our journey North towards Samawa to visit the Ancient City of Uruk (approx. 2.5 - 3 hours), a UNESCO World Heritage site. Uruk is historically significant as one of the world's first cities and the place where writing originated around 3300 BC. You will explore the archaeological remains that provided the earliest evidence of pottery and cuneiform tablets. Uruk is also famously known as the home of the legendary King Gilgamesh, the hero of the oldest epic in human history. Following our visit to Uruk, we will drive to Najaf (approx. 2.5 hours) and check into the hotel. In the evening, we will take a walking tour to the area of the Shrine of Imam Ali, one of the most significant architectural and spiritual landmarks in the region. You will also have the opportunity to explore the Grand Bazaar of Najaf, famous for its vibrant atmosphere, jewelry, and traditional goods. Overnight in Najaf.

: Wadi Al-Salam, Al-Ukhaidir Fortress & Karbala
At 08:00 AM (This day we can have a more relaxed start even by 10 or 11), we begin the day by visiting Wadi Al-Salam (The Valley of Peace) in Najaf, recognized as the largest cemetery in the world and a site of immense spiritual and historical scale. Afterward, we will drive towards Karbala (approx. 1.5 - 2 hours). Our first stop in the area will be the Al-Ukhaidir Fortress ( Currently this site is closed for restoration but it is possible that it would be opened by the end of this season, it can also be cancelled to give more time for the shrines and visits of religious sites. Including Kufa, which holds one of the first mosques in Mesopotamia.), a magnificent Abbasid-era limestone castle. You will explore its unique architectural innovation, including its grand courtyards, residential quarters, and ancient mosque. Later in the afternoon, we will head to the heart of the city for a walking tour between the Shrines of Imam Hussain and his brother Abbas. During the tour, you will receive a detailed historical explanation of the Battle of Karbala and the deep cultural significance of these landmarks. Overnight in Karbala.

: Ancient Babylon & The Arch of Ctesiphon
At 09:00 AM, we depart for the legendary city of Babylon (approx. 1.5 - 2 hours), a UNESCO World Heritage site. You will explore the reconstructed Ishtar Gate, the Procession Street, and the original foundations of the real Ishtar Gate. The tour includes a special entrance to the Old Temples, the iconic Lion of Babylon, the Labyrinth (Maze), and both the Northern and Southern Palaces, including the historic chamber where Alexander the Great passed away. We will then drive up the hill to visit one of the former Governmental Palaces built during the previous regime, where you will have special access to the upper floors for a panoramic view of the ruins. Afterward, we head toward Baghdad (approx. 1.5 - 2 hours), stopping to visit Taq Kasra (The Arch of Ctesiphon) (Here can be added the visit for Salman Pak (Salman the Persian), as his shrine is just beside the Taq.). This architectural marvel is the largest single-span vault of unreinforced brickwork in the world and served as the royal capital of the Parthian and Sasanian empires. We will conclude the tour by witnessing the sunset from the nearby panorama building before completing the drive to your hotel in Baghdad. Overnight in Baghdad.

: Old Baghdad Heritage Tour & The Iraq Museum
At 07:00 AM, we begin our day with a traditional Baghdadi breakfast of Qaimer and Kahi (thick cream and pastry). We then embark on a comprehensive tour of Old Baghdad, starting with a walk through Al-Rasheed Street to explore the vibrant local markets, including Al-Safafeer (the copper market), Souq Al-Sarai (the stationery market), and the famous Al-Mutanabbi Street (the historic book market). Our journey through history continues with a visit to the Mustansiriya Madrasa, one of the oldest Islamic universities in the world. We will then enjoy a boat ride on the Tigris River, followed by a stop at the Statue of Al-Mutanabbi for a historical briefing on the great poet. In the afternoon(Museum Closes by 1 PM unless it is on a Friday, the order of this day needs to be flipped.), we head to The Iraq Museum (approx. 20–30 minutes transfer depending on traffic). You will wander through its world-class galleries, taking a journey through the civilizations of Mesopotamia from prehistoric times to the Islamic era. During our tour of Old Baghdad, we will stop for a traditional treat at the historic Al-Shahbender Cafe and the famous Haj Zbala Juice Shop. The evening is yours to enjoy free time for dinner or a relaxing visit to a local café. Overnight in Baghdad.

: Baghdad Religious & Historic Landmarks Tour
After breakfast, we dedicate this day to visiting the most significant spiritual and architectural landmarks in Baghdad. Our tour begins with the Al-Kadhimiya Mosque, known for its majestic golden domes, followed by a visit to the Abu Hanifa Mosque and the nearby ruins of the Nizamiyya Madrasa, one of the oldest institutions of higher learning in the Islamic world. We will then proceed to the Shrine of Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani, a site of great spiritual importance, and continue to the Abbasid Palace (This will be in the day prior as it is in Old Baghdad area), a stunning example of 12th-century architecture overlooking the Tigris. The tour also includes a visit to the Al-Rahman Mosque, one of the city's largest mosque projects, and the historic Buratha Mosque, which holds deep significance in local tradition. Later, we will drive to the outskirts of Baghdad (approx. 45 minutes) to visit the Tomb of Salman Al-Farsi(Removing this from here as it is included in day 6) (Salman the Persian) in Al-Mada'in. Throughout the day, we will explore the rich history and diverse religious heritage that has shaped Baghdad over the centuries. Overnight in Baghdad.

: Samarra, Hatra & Mosul
At 07:00 AM, we begin our journey North to Samarra (approx. 2 hours), a UNESCO World Heritage site. You will explore the magnificent Abbasid Caliphate architecture, including the iconic Malwiya (Twisted Minaret), the Great Mosque of Samarra, and the Lake Palace, witnessing the artistic relics of the golden age of the Abbasids. Next, we continue our drive to the ancient city of Hatra (approx. 3 hours). Hatra is a unique UNESCO site that served as a major religious and commercial center along the caravan trade routes and was one of the first Arab states established outside the Arabian Peninsula. You will marvel at its well-preserved temples and grand stone architecture that blend Hellenistic and Roman influences with Eastern decorative features. After the tour, we will head to Mosul (approx. 2 hours). Upon arrival, we will check into the hotel. In the evening, you will enjoy a traditional dinner featuring Mosul's famous dish, Lahm Baajeen. Overnight in Mosul.

: Mosul Old City & Post-War Recovery Tour
At 08:00 AM, we begin our exploration of the Old City of Mosul. We will witness the remarkable reconstruction efforts led by UNESCO, focusing on the Al-Nuri Mosque, the iconic Al-Hadba Minaret, and Al-Tahira Church. We will walk through the historic neighborhoods that witnessed the final and most intensive battles against ISIS, gaining a deep understanding of the city's recent history. During the tour, you will have the unique opportunity to hear personal stories from local residents who lived through the conflict and are now rebuilding their lives. The afternoon is yours for free time to explore the local markets of Mosul. In the evening, we will visit a unique local café for a traditional music performance. This building has a complex history, having served as a hospital during the conflict, and now stands as a symbol of the city's cultural revival. Overnight in Mosul.

: Nineveh Plains & Return to Baghdad
In the early morning, we depart for the Plains of Nineveh (approx. 45 minutes – 1 hour). We will visit the town of Bahzani, where you will enjoy a traditional breakfast with a local Christian family, hearing their personal stories and learning about the deep history of the region's diverse communities. The tour continues with a visit to some of the ancient Yazidi temples in the town, providing insight into one of the world's oldest belief systems. Afterward, we begin our journey back to Baghdad (approx. 5.5 – 6 hours). Upon arrival, you will check into the hotel for your final night in the capital. Overnight in Baghdad.

: Free Day in Baghdad
Today is a free day for you to explore Baghdad at your own pace. You can revisit your favorite spots in the old city, such as Al-Mutanabbi Street, or spend time in the modern districts like Karrada and Mansour for shopping and experiencing the city’s contemporary lifestyle. This is also an excellent opportunity to visit any local galleries or museums you may have missed. Overnight in Baghdad.

: Departure from Baghdad
After breakfast, please complete the check-out process at the hotel. Depending on your flight schedule, you will be picked up for your private transfer to Baghdad International Airport (approx. 45 minutes – 1 hour). Our representative will assist you at the airport for your final departure.

Arrival and departure airport transfers.
Daily breakfast at the hotels.
Professional English-speaking guide for all tours, including a female guide to accompany female guests and facilitate their entry into the holy shrines, ensuring a smooth and respectful visit.
Local coordinators and specialized guides in each city to facilitate the tour.
Entrance tickets for all sites and museums mentioned as visited in the itinerary.
All tours and activities, including Shatt Al-Arab and Marshland boat trips.
Transportation by a fully air-conditioned, non-smoking coach (VIP bus with charging sockets and toilets or a modern Coaster depending on PAX).
2 nights in Basra on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
1 night in Nasiriyah on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
1 night in Najaf on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
1 night in Karbala on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
5 nights in Baghdad on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
1 night in Mosul on a Half-Board (HB) basis.
Refreshments, snacks, and logistical team services throughout the trip.
Hotel room and city taxes.
1 Pax FOC in Dbl Room.
TOUR PACKAGE EXCLUDES:
Entry Visa fees to Iraq.
International flight tickets.
Any personal expenses such as laundry, telephone calls, or mini-bar usage.
Tips for the guide and driver.
Travel insurance and medical expenses.
Any drinks or beverages during dinner.
Any additional activities or entrance fees not explicitly mentioned in the itinerary.
Important Notes & Guidelines
Hotel Check-In
Standard hotel check-in is from 2:00 PM onwards. Early check-in is subject to availability and may incur additional charges.
Religious and Cultural Etiquette
Hijab (and Abaya) is mandatory for women visiting the holy cities of Najaf, Karbala, and Al-Kadhimiyah. Our female team will be there to assist you with the suitable attire.
Men are not allowed to wear shorts inside the holy shrines; long trousers are required.
Cameras are not permitted inside the shrines of Najaf, Karbala, and Al-Kadhimiyah.
Mobile phones are allowed inside these shrines, but photography must be discreet and respectful.
Passport Restrictions
Passports containing Israeli entry stamps are not permitted for travel in Iraq. Please verify your documentation thoroughly prior to arrival.
Guests must always have their passport on them, the passport with the visa sticker.
Museum and Site Access
National Museum (Baghdad): Closed every Saturday & Sunday.  (Currently undermaintenance.)
Baghdadi Museum: Closed every Saturday and Tuesday.
Basra Museum, Al-Mustansiriyah School, Abbasid Palace, and Martyr Monument: Closed on Fridays and Saturdays.
Qishla Clock: Accessible only on Fridays; full access is not available on other days. (partial access throughout all days)
Site Accessibility Disclaimer
While we strive to provide full access to all scheduled sites, we are not liable for unforeseen circumstances (e.g., security restrictions, sudden closures) that may prevent entry to specific archaeological or cultural locations.
Photography & Prohibited Items
Photography or filming of police, military personnel, or security vehicles is strictly prohibited.
Drones are banned throughout the entirety of Iraq.
Power banks may be confiscated at airport security checkpoints. Please pack accordingly.
Financial & Currency Information
Each traveler is allowed to carry up to $5,000 (or 130g of gold) without declaration. Amounts between $5,000 and $10,000 require customs declaration.
Cash is king: Most stores do not accept cards. It is best to bring all the cash you need.
USD Notes: The most preferred notes are $100 and $50. Please ensure they are the 2013 series or newer, as older series may be rejected or exchanged at a lower value. Currency: 1$ = 1,320 IQD (Official) / Approx. 1,500 IQD (Market).
Tipping & Souvenirs
Tipping is optional. For hotel/airport luggage assistance, it should not exceed 5,000 IQD. For our staff, you may follow your own country's tradition.
Antiques and souvenirs must be placed in checked luggage. If carried in hand luggage, they may be confiscated by airport security.

◆ At dawn, we will head to Chibayesh and have a marshland 
experience.  
◆ Local breakfast in the reed house with a local family.  
◆ Followed by a sightseeing tour in numerous floating villages - the 
Gardens of Eden (birds, fishes, buffalos,  reed, plants, and meeting 
the people of Ahwar). It is one of the largest ecosystems in the world 
and a UNESCO world heritage site. 
◆ After the tour, the lunch will be a meal of a special kind of fish in Iraq 
which lives only in the marshlands. The lunch wil l take place in the 
reed house - Al Mudhif. 
◆ Stories from local people “Al Madan” who have adapted to life on 
the water over the centuries. 
◆ After that, we will drive back to Baghdad or an overnight stay in 
Chibayesh. 
 
For the designed itinerary for you: 600$ without an overnight stay 
650$ with an overnight stay

/    
◆ 7 AM Start the day with a thick-cream and pastry breakfast (Qaimer 
and Kahi). 
◆ Old Baghdad tour via Al Rasheed street, visiting various local 
markets such as the copper market “Al Safafeer”, Souq Al Sarai - 
the stationary market, Books market “Al Mutanabbi street” and 
antiques market “Khan Al Mudalal”. 
◆ Visit heritage sites such as Madrasa Mustansiriya School and the 
Abbasid Palace. 
◆ This tour includes a boat ride activity at the Tigr is river and an 
explanation about the statue of the poet Al - Mutanabbi. 
◆ Old Baghdad offers many local food restaurants along Hayder 
Khana street, such as Kubba Al Sarai, Oum Kalthoum Shawarma or 
any other of your favourites. We also will grab a treat from  both Al 
Shahbender cafe and Haj Zbala Juice shop. 
◆ Free time in the afternoon to explore the modern parts of Baghdad.  
Overnight: Baghdad / night 1.

/ 
◆ After breakfast, we will head to Babylon, a UNESCO world heritage 
site. 
◆ We will see the historical city, rebuilt Ishtar Gate, procession street, 
the foundations of the real Ishtar Gate, special entrance to the old 
temples, the lion of Babylon, the maze, southern & northern palaces, 
the place where Alexander the Great passed away.  
◆ We then will drive up the hill to see one of the governmental palaces 
that was built during the past regime time with special access to the 
upper floors. 
◆ Traditional lunch options that you can choose from.  
◆ Time to visit Birs Nimrud, visiting The Ziggurat of Borsippa known 
as the “Tongue Tower”. Many think it is the biblical “tower of 
Babylon”. This was an important ancient city of Sumer and has a 
religious edifice in honor of the god Nabu. 
◆ Head back to Baghdad. 
Overnight: Baghdad / night 2.

/ 
◆ 7 30 AM After breakfast we will head to Samarra to visit the beautiful 
Abbasid caliphate architecture and artistic relics, twisted minaret, 
lake palace, and the great mosque of Samarra. This historical city is 
a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 
◆ After that, we will drive back to Baghdad. 
Overnight: Baghdad / night 3.  
 
For the designed itinerary of 3 Days for you: 750$

city.

and

Hadbaa
 
Minaret.

their

and
 
history.

addition
 
to

beautiful

city.

: - ARRIVAL SALALAH.  
On arrival at Salalah Airport, Meet & greet outside the airport then 
transfer to the Hotel. Check-in at chosen Hotel

: Half day Salalah city tour- maximum 4 hours. 
Breakfast at the hotel & proceed via the bird sanctuary at ‘Al Balid ‘to visit “The Museum of 
the Frankincense Land”. The Museum, opened in 2006 within the ancient harbor of ‘Al Balid’, 
houses many an artifact about the rich cultural history of the ‘Dhofar Region’. One Hall 
depicting the Frankincense trail history of the Sultanate, along with many audio/video 
presentations of the Omani Renaissance since 1970, fascinates the visitor to this site. A 
complete history of the Maritime trade & ship building industry of Oman could be 
experienced in a second hall, with meticulously carved replicas of the ancient boats & ships, 
of the Omani Maritime trade. Drive through lush green plantation of vegetables & fruits & 
make a brief stop to taste the fresh coconut water drink at ‘ Fruit boutiques’ (at own cost) 
lining the streets within the periphery of the old Salalah town (Haffah ). Photo stop at the 
impressive Shanfari Mosque. View the Official Palace of the Sultan (Al Husn Palace) & stroll 
through the old Haffah souk, famous for the sale of high-quality Frankincense & numerous 
other Dhofari traditional souvenirs. Visit the new Salalah  region of the gold/silver souk, with 
ample opportunity for shopping, before we return to the hotel.

Daily excursions options in Salalah 
 
Option 01: HISTRORICAL DHOFAR-HALF DAY SALALAH EAST (Duration: approx. 4 Hrs.) 
 
The excursion begins with a visit to the old fishing village of 'Taqa', famous for the 
manufacture of 'Dried Sardines' & with its traditional & old typical 'Dhofari Houses'. Visit the 
century old 'Castle', the official residence of the former 'Wali' of the region & obtain a 
glimpse into the rich history of the region. Continue onto the ancient ruins of the Palace of 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
 
 
 
the legendary Queen Sheeba (Khor Rohri) believed to have been the hub & harbour for the 
shipping of Frankincense, for export to the rest of the Arabian Peninsula. A picturesque 
drive then leads you to 'Mirbat', The ancient capital of 'Dhofar', which in the 9th century 
traded in frankincense, horses & slaves. Stroll through the streets lined with old Omani mud 
houses & visit Dhofar's best known historic site – the 'twin-domed Bin Ali Tomb & 
Mosque…a classic example of medieval architecture. On our way back to the hotel, we 
explore the gardens of 'Ayn Razat', beautifully laid out amidst the tranquil lush mountains & 
nourished every day of the year by natural underground spring water. Return to the hotel 
by late noon.

Option 02: JEBEL SAFARI (JABEL SAMHAN) TOUR 
 
We leave the Hotel in the morning by 4X4 vehicles, on a full day safari into the Dhofar 
mountain range. Driving through the scenic village of Taqa we make a photo stop at the 
village for a panoramic view from above a cliff, well known as Taqah Plateau. We then drive 
into the 'ever green Wadi Darbat' for a relaxing stroll along the Wadi bed, surrounded by 
herds of Camels, Goats & Cattle. In the Khareef season (monsoon period), one could also 
witness an almost 100m natural Water-Fall, spreading its ‘tentacles’ into numerous lakes & 
lush green Vegetation. Our next stop is one of the worlds largest Sink Holes (211 m deep & 
150 m in diameter), situated at Tawi Attair – also known as the “Well of Birds”, who 
frequent this location, the year through. Continue journey into the mountain range of Jebel 
Samhan to a breathtaking plateau at a height of almost 1700m. This location is commonly 
known as the 'Grand Canyon' of Dhofar, gives one a complete view of the east coast to the 
one side & the vast 'Qara' mountain range to the other. The group will be hosted here to 
sumptuous picnic lunch. After lunch we continue our journey from the plateau into the 
adjacent 'Qara' mountain range & drive through scenic Jebali villages & landscape, with 
numerous photo stops at interesting locations. Return to Salalah by evening. 
Services included: Water on Board

Option 03: HALF DAY SALALAH WEST (Duration: approx. 4 Hrs.) 
After breakfast we depart on a half day tour of Salalah West & drive to the 'Qara' 
mountains. On a road steadily winding up a steep incline, herds of Camels & Cattle are a 
common sight & more often an obstruction to vehicular traffic! Visit the ancient tomb of 
'Prophet Job' situated in the scenic green mountains of the Salalah Plains. Proceed to the 
beach of Mughsail where the white sands touch the deep blue of the ocean & at high tide, 
where waves burst through the natural titanic 'Blow Holes', at the far end of the 'Rocky 
beach' with a cave-like entrance through the 'Dragon Rock'. We thereafter continue along 
the 'Hair-pin-bend' road towards Yemen, with its white cliffs on either side, to see the 
historical 'Frankincense trees' growing wild, deep down in the valleys, dotting the dry & 
craggy countryside. Stop for a walk into the valleys to smell the 'Holy Incense' amidst the 
scenic view of the region. On our return journey we make a photo stop at the lagoon at 
Mughsail where migratory birds – flamingos & others – are a common sight. Return to the 
hotel by early afternoon.
